newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Christmas Eve bombs kill three S.Africans.
newsitem.headline: Christmas Eve bombs kill three S.Africans.

text.p: Three pipe bombs blasted throngs of Christmas shoppers in a small South African town on Tuesday, killing two children and an adult and wounding up to 80 people, police said.
A spokesman told Reuters police were looking for three suspects who fled the bombing scene in Worcester, 90 km (55 miles) northeast of Cape Town, in a red car.
"We have no clue to the motive," he said. A reward of half-a-million rand ($107,000) has been offered for information.
Two of the bombs exploded at a pharmacy and one at a supermarket, both packed with customers doing last-minute Christmas shopping.
Hospital staff said an adult was killed instantly by one of the blasts and two children, one of them aged six, died later from their injuries.
They said about 30 people had been discharged after treatment for light wounds but other casualties, including children, had been sent to better equipped hospitals in Cape Town.
Most of the casualties were people of mixed race descent, known in South Africa as Coloureds.
"The bombs have caused a huge commotion here," said Frans Krige, a doctor at Worcester hospital. "No one can understand why anyone would want to plant bombs here."
Worcester is a sleepy town in a fruit and vineyard area surrounded by picturesque mountains.
The owner of the pharmacy said he was standing about five metres (yards) away from one of the blasts at his shop.
"It was chaos. It was like a massive firecracker, everyone started screaming and running around," he said.
President Nelson Mandela's African National Congress urged the police to do all in their power to find those responsible.
"This can only be the work of enemies of peace and goodwill," a statement said.
The last major bombing in South Africa was carried out by right-wing whites who set off a series of explosions ahead of historic all-race elections in April 1994, killing 20 people.
Some rightwingers still refuse to accept majority rule and are pressing for an independent state for whites within South Africa.
